name: Rehum
overview: Rehum was a male figure noted for his leadership role in supervising the Levites as they repaired the wall during the post-exilic reconstruction of Jerusalem. Though his tribal affiliation is not specified, he is recognized in Scripture for this practical service. He is also mentioned among the signatories of a sealed covenant document, indicating his involvement in the community's formal commitments.
namesAndTitles: The name Rehum means '[he] is compassionate' in Hebrew. This proper name is recorded without indication that it was divinely given, reflecting a personal attribute or family hope rather than a direct theological title.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Rehum was the father of Bani. Beyond this, no other family relationships are detailed in the biblical text concerning him.
scriptureSignificance: Rehum's significance lies in his administrative role during the critical period of Jerusalem's restoration, particularly in overseeing the Levites' efforts to repair the city wall. His inclusion among those who sealed the covenant highlights his standing within the post-exilic community, marking him as a committed participant in the spiritual and physical rebuilding of God's people. This positions him as a faithful servant contributing to the preservation and renewal of Israel.
